featured_reviews.name: Moumita Roy
featured_reviews.review_text: Jeevan Boarding House is a hidden gem in Chembur for anyone looking for simple, homely food at an unbeatable price. For just ₹100, you get a complete meal starting from chutney and accompaniments all the way to a sweet dish. The food is fresh, tasty, and feels like a home-cooked meal. The service is quick, and the overall experience is great value for money. A must-visit if you’re looking for an affordable and satisfying meal.

featured_reviews.name: ashish kumar
featured_reviews.review_text: Good food. Enjoyed the fresh south indian dinner delicacies in banana leaf...cost for each only Rs 110/- and legendary outlet since 1962. featured_reviews.name: Saakshi Shinde
featured_reviews.review_text:
We had a special southindian lunch served by Jeevan Thali at our office in marol. The thali had absolutely amazing and truly satisfying. The meal was a perfect balance of flavors, textures, and authenticity. From the moment it was served, the aroma itself was enough to make me excited to dig in.

The thali included a variety of dishes like sambar, rasam, different vegetable curries, chutneys, all served with soft rice, crispy papad, and perfectly made chapatis, puranpoli, paysam. Each item had its own distinct taste—rich, flavorful, and well-seasoned without being too heavy.

What stood out the most was the freshness and authenticity of the preparation. The service was also warm and attentive, adding to the overall experience.

Overall, it was a wholesome, delicious, and fulfilling meal that truly represents the essence of South Indian cuisine. Definitely a must-try for anyone who loves traditional and flavorful food!

featured_reviews.name: PARIMAL BORKAR
featured_reviews.review_text:

Food is amazing, staff is best, the way of serving is different that they use Banana leaf for every unlimited food by heart serving the staff. Pineapple Bhaji was different in taste, it tastes so good ki mood ban jaye. Rassam, curd, papad, two more Bhaji, sweet dish and everything fulfilled and make you satisfied.
So many varieties you need to visit and just taste it, menu changes day to day so please confirm the menu if you want to test pineapple Bhaji.

Because parking is on drawback.

featured_reviews.name: Akash Mande
featured_reviews.review_text: Jeevan Boarding House, Chembur is a classic South Indian restaurant with a legacy going back to 1962. The place serves simple, authentic South Indian food at very affordable prices. The taste is consistent, homely, and reminds you of old-school eateries that focus more on food than frills. Portions are satisfying, service is quick, and the atmosphere has a nostalgic charm. A must-visit for anyone who enjoys traditional South Indian meals without burning a hole in the pocket.

featured_reviews.name: Ajinkya Girmal
featured_reviews.review_text:
I recently shifted to Mumbai from Kolhapur. Being a bachelor, I’m always in search of homely food at an affordable rate, and after three months, I finally found Jeevan Boarding House simply divine taste! 🫠

Actually, I discovered this place last week on Swiggy while looking for homely food at reasonable prices  something that rarely happens on food apps. But this time, I was lucky! I ordered their thali on Swiggy, and when the parcel arrived, I was pleasantly surprised to see so many delicious dishes packed together. That was the first time I tasted their food.

Today, while returning home, I decided to visit their premises and what a pleasant surprise! Polite service, tempting South Indian dishes, from tangy tomato curry to sweet rice kheer simply divine! 😋 Only in 100 Rs serving on banana leaf

Highly recommend

featured_reviews.name: Gokulraj
featured_reviews.review_text:
Jeevan Boarding House in Chembur is a great spot if you're looking for delicious South Indian meals on a budget!

The ambiance is simple but pleasant, and the food is absolutely worth it.

It’s conveniently located—just a 1-minute walk from Chembur station—making it super easy to reach.

Their meals (Thali) are priced at just ₹90, which is a steal for the quality and quantity you get. Everything served beyond the basic meal is charged extra, but still very affordable.

Meals are served traditionally on a banana leaf, which adds to the authentic experience. The taste is amazing—especially their pineapple sweet and payasam, which are both top notch. You definitely won’t leave hungry, as the portions are more than enough!

Be prepared to wait if you visit during peak hoursit gets quite crowded after 1 PM, but the food is worth the wait. 😄

Highly recommended for anyone craving wholesome South Indian food!

featured_reviews.name: Pavan Sharma
featured_reviews.review_text:
First Review:Nice food

Second Review
India Bistro in Chembur offers a lively vibe and inventive modern Indian fare .The complimentary pani puri is a fun highlight: crispy puris come with pre-filled syringes of tangy pani and sweet chutney for self-injection—interactive, hygienic, and playful. The puris stay crunchy, with balanced spicy-herby and sweet-tangy flavors. Pro tip: Add the complimentary vinegared onions and a squeeze of fresh lemon. The extra acidity and crunch elevate it to near-chaat level—zesty, layered, and addictive.Standouts include:
• Crimson Dusk mocktail: Vibrant orange-pomegranate-mint blend with grenadine and lemonade—refreshing, balanced, and sunset-hued.
• Gulabo: Elegant rose-infused dish with subtle floral notes—light, aromatic, and sophisticated.
• Dahi Kabab: Creamy yogurt kebabs with crisp exterior and melt-in-mouth interior—rich yet light, perfectly spiced, and highly addictive. For a normal person it's always a question to put the curd in such a creative space.
Minor disappointing personal aspect—the apricot kofta was indeed a unique gem at India Bistro Chembur, with its creamy malai-style koftas stuffed with fresh apricot flavour for that subtle sweet-tangy surprise in every bite. It added a lovely fruity twist to the classic kofta gravy, making it stand out from the usual options. From last few visits it has vanished. Another disappointing issue is no sugerfree option in mocktail and in sweets. Though Rasmalai here is almost with out suger.
Generous portions, attentive service, and no pretension make it a go-to for flavorful, enjoyable meals in Chembur.

featured_reviews.name: Nikhil Kamath
featured_reviews.review_text:
Tried Shankar Mahadevan’s @malgudi.ind in Chembur during my recent Mumbai trip, a restaurant that’s become quite popular for its modern take on South Indian food. We started with the Anna Style Crispy Lotus Root, which had a tangy tamarind-heavy flavour and worked well as a snack. The much-hyped Mulbagal Dosa, though visually interesting with its parcel-like shape, tasted fairly ordinary. The Davangere Benne Podi Dosa followed a similar route, comforting but not very memorable beyond the podi and butter.

For the main course, we ordered Sanchi’s Vegetable Stew with Appam and Veg Malabar Curry with Malabar Parotta. The curry and parotta were satisfying, but the stew felt too watery and lacked the comforting richness you expect from a good appam-stew combination.

The real standout was the Filter Kaapi Panna Cotta. Smooth, creamy, and packed with coffee and jaggery flavour, it easily ended up being the best thing on the table.

featured_reviews.name: Mridula Bhat
featured_reviews.review_text:
Visited Malgudi – Shankar Mahadevan’s Resto Café Bar recently and it’s a refreshing take on South Indian cuisine.

What stands out is how they’ve retained the comfort of familiar flavours while introducing thoughtful, modern elements, especially in their coffee menu. The filter coffee variations are genuinely interesting.

The space itself has a warm, slightly nostalgic vibe.

Food quality was solid. Service was courteous.

We highly recommend Ghee Podi Thatthe Idli, Mulbagal Dosa, Mushroom Ghee Roast with Neer Dosa, Sri Lankan Tamil Curry with Idiyappam, Bisi Bele Bhaath and the soulful and delicious Sheera for dessert.

For drinks, we tried Mango Matcha Beery and Iced Kaapi (this had jaggery and ghee) and was delicious!

Overall, it’s a place worth visiting if you’re looking to experience South Indian food in a slightly elevated setting.

featured_reviews.name: Ranjeet Singh Grover
featured_reviews.review_text:
Vaishali Garden Restaurant is conveniently located near Chembur Station. While the streets can feel quite crowded, the valet parking service is a great solution. The restaurant is situated on the first floor, which might be a concern for elderly visitors, but thankfully, there is a lift available.

The ambience is inviting both inside and outside. Being a garden restaurant, it offers an open terrace seating option, while the indoor area has a cozy atmosphere, making it ideal for any season. The aroma of spices as we entered heightened our appetite.

We began our meal with the welcome munchies,,, boiled peanuts, which were a nice touch. For starters, we ordered chicken tikka and paneer tikka, both of which were flavorful. Since we opted for a Chinese theme for the evening, we followed up with noodles, fried rice, and dry Manchurian gravy. Despite the restaurant being jam-packed, with people even waiting outside, the service was impressively prompt.

The quality of the food was excellent, and the service deserves full marks. While Vaishali Garden Restaurant falls into the premium category and might seem a bit pricey, it’s worth every penny. We made sure to reserve our table in advance for 8:30 PM, which ensured a seamless dining experience.

I’m sharing a photo of a clock crafted on the backside of a kadhai,…a unique and artistic touch that adds to the charm of the place.

There are so many options that you simply can't try everything in one visit—which gives you every reason to keep coming back.

If you're nearby in Tilak Nagar, make sure to visit and experience it for yourself. Wishing them continued success and many more happy customers ahead. 🤭🔥

Ordered from here for the first time and it was worth every bit.

We were looking to have some sarson saag and dal tadka with makke di roti on this windy sunday morning for lunch. Came across ludhiana junction online and decided to order home delivery.

Rakesh was helpful on the phone and took my order.

Food arrived within the hour, hot! The dal and especially the sarson saag was exceptional. Makke di roti was of decent size with ghee. Also received extra ghee, punjabi achaar and jaggery in small containers. That was the cherry on top. Not a lot of restaurants send that. Thank you.

One suggestion, pack indian breads in aluminium foil so that the ghee stays inside. The butter paper in which it was wrapped had soaked up all the ghee on rotis and was oily all over.

I was pleasantly surprised to have a 10% discount as the order was above ₹1000.
Thanks again!

I would be happy to order from here more often.

Had one of the finest dining experiences at Ludhiana Junction, Chembur. This restaurant truly deserves its reputation as one of the top-listed dining destinations in the area. From the warm hospitality and elegant ambience to the exceptional quality of food, everything was absolutely outstanding.
What impressed us the most was the incredible variety of both vegetarian and non-vegetarian starters. The menu offers something for every palate, and each dish was prepared with great attention to taste and presentation. Among the non-vegetarian starters, the Hara Bhara Kebab, Prawns, Chicken, and Fish preparations were simply phenomenal. The fish and prawns were undoubtedly the stars of the evening—perfectly cooked, fresh, flavourful, and among the best starters we have had in Chembur.
The main course was equally impressive. Their Thai Curry was exceptionally delicious, rich in flavour, beautifully balanced, and one of the best we've tasted in a long time. It was the perfect complement to the wonderful starters.
To end the meal on a sweet note, we indulged in their delightful range of desserts. The variety offered was excellent, and every dessert we tried was fresh, beautifully presented, and absolutely satisfying. It was the perfect conclusion to an unforgettable dining experience.
Ludhiana Junction has successfully combined great food, excellent service, and a welcoming atmosphere to create a memorable experience. Whether you're a vegetarian or a non-vegetarian food lover, this place is a must-visit. Highly recommended for family dinners, celebrations, and anyone looking for one of the best dining experiences in Chembur. Will definitely be visiting again! ⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐

featured_reviews.review_text:
Coastal Fusion in Chembur is one of those rare restaurants where everything — from the food to the ambience — just falls into place.

I visited recently and started with their Fish Thali, which came loaded with Bangda, Mandeli, Bombil, and Surmai. The flavors were genuinely homestyle and the freshness of the fish was evident in every bite. After that, the Dhaba Style Chicken brought that earthy, slow-cooked richness that you don't find easily anymore. The Kala Masala Chicken Starter stole the show for me — well-spiced, deeply flavored, and gone before I knew it. There's also a Maharashtrian Veg Platter for vegetarians that doesn't feel like an afterthought.

Dessert was Aamras and Gajar Halwa — both done well, a satisfying end to a great meal.

The restaurant is spacious and comfortable, making it a great choice for families and groups. The service was warm and the whole experience felt very genuine.

Highly recommended for anyone craving authentic Maharashtrian and coastal flavors in Chembur.

Pleasant Ambience and Excellent Service, but Food Could Be Better

I recently dined at Hotel Grand Central in Chembur and had a mixed experience. The first thing that stands out about this restaurant is its inviting ambience. The decor is tasteful, creating a cozy and comfortable atmosphere that makes you feel at ease as soon as you step in.

However, while the ambience is impressive, the food was just okay. The dishes were decent but didn't quite live up to my expectations in terms of flavor. That said, the variety on the menu is good, so there’s plenty to choose from.

On the positive side, the service at Hotel Grand Central is top-notch. The staff is attentive, courteous, and quick to respond to any requests. The cleanliness of the restaurant is also commendable, which adds to the overall pleasant dining experience.

In summary, Hotel Grand Central is a great place if you're looking for a nice setting and excellent service. If the food quality improves a bit, it could easily become a top choice in Chembur.

This review offers a balanced perspective, highlighting both the strengths and areas for improvement at Hotel Grand Central.

featured_reviews.name: Rohit Sharma
featured_reviews.review_text:
Visited this place for lunch today and honestly had a mixed experience.
Food: ⭐⭐
Service: ⭐
We ordered chicken biryani with sol kadhi. From the very first sip, we felt the sol kadhi was unusually spicy. We called the waiter only to give genuine feedback — we weren’t even planning to return it, just leave it aside and order something else. However, the waiter insisted that “it is made like this only.” We informed him that this wasn’t our first time having it here and that we know how it normally tastes.
After some time, he came back and asked us to order something else. When we chose orange juice, he commented that we should cancel it because we might again find it bitter — which felt quite insulting, especially when we were simply sharing feedback. To make matters worse, a customer sitting next to us also advised against ordering it because they didn’t like it either.
This behavior from the service staff was disappointing and unprofessional. The chicken biryani itself was good, but the argument and attitude completely spoiled the overall experience.
Hoping the management pays attention to customer feedback and improves service etiquette.
